hypotheses.reasoning: index-worker partition 10 is stuck on a single malformed message msg-416639 (offset 776449). Every attempt fails with 'JSON parse error: unexpected token \u0000 at position 1708', which indicates a corrupted payload containing a NUL byte. The consumer nacks and redelivers it with no max-retries configured, so it retries forever (attempt 8 at #158 through attempt 33 at #219 and beyond) and blocks the partition. Consumer lag on partition 10 then climbs from 45s (#187) to 828s (#309) and about 14k messages. Batches were processing normally with ~100ms lag until #147, so the onset is this message. Index-worker CPU is normal because the consumer is idle-looping on one message, not saturated. The search-api 'timed out waiting for downstream confirmation' errors (#208, #237, #259, #275, #284, #310) are downstream symptoms: search-api is waiting on index updates that never land. catalog-db, redis and catalog-svc show no faults; the GC pause (#125) and the seq-scan audit_log query (#129) are minor and predate the stall. The first attempt number visible in the logs is 8, so the earliest failures are not in the retained window. I did not confirm the producer of the bad record.

Alternative reading: the NUL-byte corruption is itself a data integrity problem in the catalog update record written upstream, which explains why the message cannot be parsed. It does not explain the stall by itself. The missing retry cap is what turns one bad record into a backlog, so poison_message is the better fit for the impact.

verdict.recommendedAction: Immediately move msg-416639 (partition 10, offset 776449) to a dead-letter queue or skip past that offset so partition 10 resumes, then let the backlog drain. Configure a max-retry limit with DLQ routing on catalog.updates so a single bad message cannot block a partition. Trace the producer that emitted a payload with a NUL byte at position 1708 and fix input validation there. Once the lag is clear, re-index the affected products (for example p-2127, p-2147, p-2165) that search-api marked failed.
